action: WordPress.org recommends updating your sites immediately (Dashboard > Updates > Update Now); sites with automatic background updates will update automatically.
exec: WordPress runs a large share of company websites, and this release fixes an unauthenticated flaw the project says could lead to remote code execution.
plain: WordPress released an update; Patchstack counts twenty fixes, including one that lets someone without an account gain higher access and possibly run code. The project recommends updating immediately.

key_findings: Unauthenticated privilege escalation via Template Part block attributes that the post says could lead to remote code execution.
Multisite: a site Administrator can take over a Super Admin account via Customizer menu previews.
Two SQL injection fixes (WP_Meta_Query and Customizer changeset front-page setting) and unauthenticated stored XSS via comment shortcode attributes.
The post does not mention exploitation in the wild.
recommendations: Update immediately; automatic background updates begin on sites that support them.

summary: WordPress 7.1.5, released November 18, is a security release; Patchstack counts twenty fixes. They include unauthenticated privilege escalation through Template Part block attributes that the project says could lead to remote code execution, two SQL injections, a Multisite Super Admin takeover and stored XSS in comments. The project recommends updating immediately and its post does not mention exploitation.
title: WordPress 7.1.5 security release fixes unauthenticated privilege escalation and SQL injection

validation.note: WordPress.org release post and GBHackers agree on release date, the Template Part flaw, SQL injection and XSS fixes. Neither gives CVE ids. Patchstack (18 Nov) also lists the fixes, states no CVE ids had been assigned at publication and does not report exploitation.

review.note: figure: '20 items' was not stated by the WordPress post (Patchstack says twenty fixes), reworded with attribution and evidence quote; action advice now names WordPress.org; added source published days

evidence.quote: It is a security release with twenty fixes, eighteen of which we have added to the Patchstack database as vulnerabilities
